title: Contract v3.1 — land the two unadopted review fixes and the three v3 regressions
objective: Amend the claude_code_mobile_bootstrap_remediation contract from v3.0.0 to v3.1.0 so that it (a) restores and asserts partial-installer-run safety, (b) makes the SessionStart self-heal time budget a measured preflight obligation rather than an assumption, (c) replaces a C11B assertion that is guaranteed to fail once the remediation merges, (d) actually verifies Context7 reachability and defines rebuild_observed as a measurable, and (e) records the brokered-path evidence behind the operator decision to retain the cloud_activation lane. This plan edits the contract document only; it does not modify install.sh, the SessionStart hook, or any adapter code.
success_criteria: C1_SESSIONSTART_SELF_HEAL carries a failures block again, satisfying governance.require and repairing the false internal_consistency: PASS claim in v3.0.0
C1 declares partial_installer_run_is_safe_to_rerun as an invariant and installer_steps_verified_idempotent as a precondition
P1_REPOSITORY_PREFLIGHT emits installer_steps_verified_idempotent and BLOCKs on a non-idempotent install.sh step
P1 emits warm_install_seconds, sessionstart_prefix_seconds and available_self_heal_budget_seconds
P1 BLOCKs when available_self_heal_budget_seconds is below warm_install_seconds, halting C1 with a required-timeout-increase report
C11B no longer compares observed_governance_revision against the frozen INPUT_EXECUTION_SHA
C11B validates egress to api.context7.io with an exact machine-checkable expectation
C11B defines rebuild_observed with a stated measurement method rather than an undefined boolean
C11A records the brokered-path evidence and C11B records that PENDING_NEXT_SESSION is the expected resting state until broker deployment
The v3.1 contract parses as YAML and passes the five-fix assertion script without manual inspection

disconfirming_questions: If install.sh steps are already idempotent, does A1 add anything beyond documentation? Yes — an unasserted property silently regresses the first time someone adds a non-guarded step, and C12 has no test for it today.

Could the A2 measurement itself mutate the live environment? Only if HOME isolation fails; P2 verified RECEIPT derives from $HOME and --governance overrides GOV_DIR, and the plan requires a disposable workspace clone.
Is warm-run timing stable enough to gate C1 on? It is not, on a cold cache — which is why the failure is BLOCKED with a report rather than an automatic timeout bump.
Does A3 simply move the goalposts so C11B always passes? No — the staleness check still fails when a session runs a receipt older than live main, which is the real defect it was meant to catch.
Will the A4 probe ever pass? Not until the broker is deployed. A5 records exactly that, and PENDING_NEXT_SESSION is already non-blocking for V1 and I1.
Does retaining the lane contradict the evidence in P4? It is an operator decision taken with that evidence in hand; A5 preserves the evidence so it is not silently re-litigated.

Does editing the contract without touching code leave the fixes unproven? Yes, partially — A1 and A2 are only fully discharged when P1 runs against the real adapter, which the verification section states explicitly.
assumed_false_ifs: Anthropic changes SessionStart hook timeout semantics, which would invalidate the A2 budget arithmetic
A future install.sh step is added without a guard, which would falsify the A1 invariant and should then fail the new regression test
A session-side direct consumer of api.context7.io is introduced, which would make the A5 brokered-path note stale

risks.risk: A2's warm-run measurement is taken on a warm cache and under-estimates a cold-start session, letting C1 through a budget it will miss in practice
risks.mitigation: record the cache state alongside the measurement and treat the warm number as a lower bound; the BLOCKED failure names a required timeout increase rather than silently accepting the margin

risks.risk: Restoring C1.failures exposes that seven other tasks still lack the block, inviting scope creep
risks.mitigation: explicitly out of scope and listed as follow-on; the five items stay the deliverable

risks.risk: The retained cloud_activation lane parks at PENDING indefinitely and is later mistaken for an unfinished obligation
risks.mitigation: A5 records expected_until: broker_deployment_completes so the resting state is self-documenting

risks.risk: The contract is authored as YAML with no schema, so structural errors surface only at execution
risks.mitigation: the verification section runs a parse plus an explicit five-fix assertion script, which is the closest available equivalent to a schema check

risks.risk: v3.0.0 exists only in conversation, so v3.1 could silently diverge from what was reviewed
risks.mitigation: A1 creates v3.1 as a full document rather than a patch, so the committed file is the single readable source
